subject: P95 oscillation affecting BrightCart checkout API
messages:
From: Pete Liu <pete.liu@brightcart.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@brightcart.com
Date: 2027-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Checkout API p95s jumping, throughput falling (us-east-1)

Sergio —

We're seeing a pretty sharp degradation across our Redwood-backed checkout gen endpoint starting ~08:50 PDT. P95s climbed from ~600ms to ~5.8s and tail latency appears to be correlated with a drop in throughput (orders/sec fell ~40%). Attached screenshot shows the spike and our request volume. This is impacting live sessions.

Can you confirm if there's an ongoing incident on your side? Any early ideas? We'd like a timeline for mitigation and whether you recommend a fallback model/route while you triage.

Attachments: latency-dashboard.png (PNG screenshot)

—Pete
Pete Liu
Sr. SRE, BrightCart

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Pete Liu <pete.liu@brightcart.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-21T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API p95s jumping, throughput falling (us-east-1)

Pete — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. We're on it. I'm looping in Ben (SRE lead) and Marissa (product) so we can coordinate an immediate mitigation and a clear customer message.

Immediate asks from our side so we can scope impact quickly:
- Can you confirm whether requests are all going to the gen-text v2.1 model variant or mixed variants?
- Any recent rollout on your side (client-side batching/longer prompting, streaming changes)?
- If possible, share a short window (08:45-09:00) of request IDs or trace IDs — we can map to our traces.

For BrightCart: we propose a protective routing rule to steer traffic to the lower-latency model variant (v2.0-lit) while SREs triage. If Ben confirms it's safe, we'll implement a 15–30 minute protective route and monitor.

Ben/Marissa — I'm OK to send a brief standby note to Pete once we have the mitigation plan.

— Sergio Alvarez
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-07-21T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Checkout API p95s jumping, throughput falling (us-east-1)

Sergio / team — quick triage notes:
- I see the same P95 jump in our US-EAST gen cluster around 08:48. K/V cache miss rate jumped and CPU on the inference pool increased, which lines up with tokenization + kernel pressure.
- Initial hypothesis: a recent quantization tweak rolled into v2.1 reduced cache hit friendliness for certain prompt patterns; that combined with a transient fanout spike caused queueing.

Immediate mitigation we can run now (low risk):
1) Apply protective routing for BrightCart to route to v2.0-lit (lower memory footprint) — this is a config change, no infra restart.
2) Warm up KV cache on the node pool serving v2.1 by running a synthetic prefix sweep (Ben will run) — this helps if eviction is the issue.
3) If p95 remains >2.0s after 15m, we do a canary rollback of the quant change on a small slice of v2.1 traffic.

I've attached a quick logs bundle for the 08:40-09:10 window (prod-logs-20270721.zip). Ben will also stream a Grafana snapshot in the bridge.

I'll start the protective routing now and report back with delta.

— Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — good triage. A couple of product-level asks while SREs run mitigation:
- Pause any further rollout of the quantization profile to v2.1 globally until we confirm behavior on BrightCart's access patterns. We should gate the rollout and revert the most recent canary immediately to prevent broader customer impact.
- Prep a short impact analysis: expected CPU/memory delta and cost delta if we route BrightCart to v2.0-lit for an hour. This helps Sales negotiate any credits if needed.

Draft external note to BrightCart (suggested):
"Pete — we’re implementing a protective routing rule now to reduce latency and we’ll run a short KV cache warm-up. If performance does not improve within 15 minutes we will rollback the recent quantization change on a small slice of traffic. We’ll keep you updated every 15 minutes and follow with a full post-mortem within 48 hours."

If SREs confirm that warm-up + routing brings p95 back under 1.5s we'll avoid rollback. Please hold off on messaging until Sergio sends the external update.

— Marissa Cole
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

Planned next steps:
- Monitor for 15 minutes for p95 improvement.
- If p95 remains >2.0s after 15m, we will rollback the quant change on a small canary slice and notify you before switching.
- We will follow up with a full post-mortem and root cause analysis within 48 hours.

Subject: Re: Checkout API p95s jumping, throughput falling (us-east-1) — mitigation summary

Status update & close of active mitigation window:
- Timeline: protective routing applied 2027-07-21T10:02:00-07:00; KV warm-up executed 10:04; monitor window ran 10:04–10:25.
- Result: p95 for BrightCart fell from ~5.8s to ~1.2s within the 15-minute window; throughput returned to baseline.
- Actions taken: protective routing to v2.0-lit, cache warm-up, and pause on quant rollout. We did not perform a canary rollback after the routing improved metrics.

Attachments: mitigation-snapshot.png (Grafana snapshot) — shows p95 delta and queue length drop.

Immediate follow-ups (next 48 hours):
1) Product to run a focused regression test for the quantization profile on prefixes matching BrightCart patterns (Marissa).
2) Engineering to capture better eviction telemetry for v2.1 (Karthik/Ben).
3) Postmortem runbook and customer-facing RCA draft (owner: Ben) — due in 48 hours.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: interaction between the new quantization kernel and certain prefix distributions caused inefficient KV cache utilization under bursty fanout. We will confirm with additional traces.

Thanks for patience, Pete — we’ll follow up with the postmortem and any credits/contract-level impacts once we have the full analysis.

— Ben Carter
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
